did_you_know.text: Did you know? The kings of Canaan united to fight Joshua and Israel, while the Gibeonites chose a different approach: deception and a treaty.
Did you know? The Gibeonites heard about the conquest of Jericho and Ai, so they realized they had to act quickly to save themselves.
Did you know? The Gibeonites disguised themselves as travelers from a distant land, using worn-out sacks and wineskins, sandals, and clothing.
Did you know? The Israelites suspected that the messengers were not from a distant land but lived nearby, so they asked how they could make a treaty with them.
Did you know? The Gibeonites claimed that they had heard about the Lord’s deeds in Egypt and Israel’s victories over Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan.
Did you know? The text emphasizes that the Israelites accepted provisions from the Gibeonites but did not seek the Lord’s guidance before making the treaty.
Did you know? Only after three days did the Israelites discover that the Gibeonites were not from a distant land but lived nearby.
Did you know? Although the people complained against their leaders, the leaders refused to harm the Gibeonites because they had sworn an oath to them by the Lord, the God of Israel.
Did you know? As a result of the treaty, the Gibeonites were assigned to cut wood and draw water for the entire community.
Did you know? Joshua decreed that the Gibeonites would also serve at the Lord’s altar in the place He would choose, preserving the treaty while changing their status.
